html:
The Ais were an Indigenous people of the Atlantic coast of Florida, along the Indian River lagoon from about Cape Canaveral south to the St Lucie inlet. They lived by fishing, hunting and gathering shellfish, palm berries and sea grapes, and did not farm.

Spanish ships of the treasure fleet often wrecked on this coast, and the Ais took silver, captives and goods from them. In 1696 the Quaker merchant Jonathan Dickinson was shipwrecked among them, and his journal is the fullest account of their life. Like the Tequesta and Calusa to the south, they were wiped out in the 1700s by disease and by slave raids from the English Carolinas and their Indigenous allies.
